title: What qualification and training do securities sales representatives need in Japan?
description: How Japan's sales representative (gaimuin) system works: FIEA Article 64 registration, JSDA qualification exams, and renewal training every five years.
shortAnswer: In Japan, anyone who solicits or sells securities for a securities firm or bank must be registered as a sales representative (外務員, gaimuin) under Article 64 of the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act. The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) runs the qualification exams and, under delegated authority, the registration. Registered representatives must complete qualification renewal training every five years from registration, and new registrants within 180 days, or their qualification is suspended and then revoked.
keyTakeaways: FIEA Article 64(1) requires financial instruments business operators and registered financial institutions to register every officer or employee who solicits or sells covered products, whatever their job title, and Article 64(2) bars unregistered people from those duties.

The JSDA grants the sales representative qualification to people who pass its exam, and handles registration under FIEA Article 64-7, which lets the Prime Minister delegate registration work to an authorized association.
There are six qualification types. Class 2 covers products such as cash equities but not margin trading or derivatives, while Class 1 covers all securities including margin and derivatives.

Qualification renewal training is mandatory every five years from the registration date, and within 180 days for new or returning registrants. Missing it suspends the qualification, and failing to complete it during suspension revokes all qualifications.
Registration can be refused for five years after a revocation, and a representative's duties can be suspended for up to two years for legal violations or seriously inappropriate conduct.
regulator: Financial Services Agency (FSA), with registration delegated to the Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) under FIEA Article 64-7
appliesTo: Officers and employees of securities firms (financial instruments business operators) who solicit or sell securities or derivatives
Officers and employees of registered financial institutions, such as banks, who perform sales representative duties
JSDA members and special members, and the compliance staff who manage their registrations
Candidates sitting JSDA sales representative qualification exams

sections.heading: Who counts as a sales representative under Japanese law?

blocks.text: A sales representative (外務員) is any officer or employee who carries out specified sales or solicitation activities for a financial instruments business operator or registered financial institution, "勧誘員、販売員、外交員その他いかなる名称を有する者であるかを問わず" (regardless of whether they are called solicitors, salespeople, canvassers or any other name). Article 64(1) of the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (FIEA, 金融商品取引法) lists the activities, which include soliciting purchases and sales of securities, market and foreign market derivatives and over the counter derivatives ([FIEA, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/323AC0000000025)).

The JSDA summarizes it as officers and employees of its members, securities companies and banks, who sell or solicit financial instruments to customers ([JSDA overview of sales representatives](https://www.jsda.or.jp/gaimuin/gaiyou.html)). Article 64(2) is the operative ban: a firm must not let anyone other than a registered person perform sales representative duties. Under Article 64-3, a registered representative is deemed to have authority to perform all out of court acts for the firm in relation to those activities, which is why firms carry responsibility for their representatives' conduct.

sections.heading: How does someone qualify and register as a sales representative?

blocks.text: A person must pass a JSDA sales representative qualification exam and then be registered through their employing member. The JSDA explains that holding the qualification alone is not enough: to work as a sales representative a person must pass the exam, then apply for registration to the JSDA through the member firm and receive registration.

items: **Qualification:** granted to people who pass the JSDA exam. It remains valid after leaving or changing employer, unless revoked for a legal violation or similar reason. The special member Class 1, Class 2 and Class 4 qualifications are not valid as securities company qualifications.

**Registration:** recorded in the sales representative register under FIEA Article 64(1). Under Article 64-7 the Prime Minister may have an authorized financial instruments firms association carry out registration work for its members' representatives, and the JSDA states that it performs this work under delegation from the state.

**Refusal:** Article 64-2(1) requires refusal where, among other grounds, the person's registration was revoked under Article 64-5 within the past five years, or the person is already registered with another firm.

**Supervisory action:** Article 64-5 allows registration to be revoked, or duties suspended for up to two years, for legal violations in the course of the business or seriously inappropriate conduct in performing sales representative duties.

blocks.text: The JSDA describes the registration system's purpose as protecting investors by setting disqualification criteria and removing unfit representatives through revocation and other measures.

sections.heading: What types of sales representative qualification exist?

blocks.text: As at November 2026 the JSDA recognizes six qualification types, split by the business a representative may handle. The two most common for securities company staff are Class 1 (一種外務員) and Class 2 (二種外務員).

blocks.text: Firms should map each role's product scope to the qualification it requires before assigning a representative to margin or derivatives clients. A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) that records qualification class against permitted products prevents out of scope solicitation.

sections.heading: How often must sales representatives complete renewal training?

blocks.text: Registered sales representatives must, in principle, complete qualification renewal training (外務員資格更新研修) every five years from their registration date. New registrants and people registering again must, in principle, complete it within 180 days. The JSDA describes the training as mandatory, intended to secure investor trust in representatives and further raise their quality.

blocks.title: Consequences of missing renewal training (JSDA)
blocks.text: If training is not completed within the period set by JSDA rules, the sales representative qualification is suspended. If it is still not completed during the suspension period, all of the person's sales representative qualifications are revoked.

People not currently attached to a JSDA member are not required to take the training, and their qualification is not revoked for that reason. The JSDA offers the training online and asks candidates to check their system meets its operating environment requirements before starting. Firms tracking these cycles can use the methods in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

blocks.text: A member firm needs to prove, for every person in a sales or solicitation role, that they were qualified, registered and current on renewal training at the time of each customer interaction. The table below is an original, illustrative mapping. JSDA rules set the binding detail.

blocks.text: Firms often add in-house training on top of the JSDA scheme, for example on [anti money laundering under the FSA guidelines](/regulations/japan-fsa-aml-cft-guidelines-training) and customer data handling under the [APPI](/regulations/japan-appi-employee-training). See [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) for record structure.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each sales role to the products it may handle, the qualification class that permits them and the renewal training cycle, in one framework. The 180 day and five year deadlines become tracked assessment points, so a firm can show at any date which representatives were qualified, registered and current for the business they handled.

faqs.q: Does a JSDA sales representative qualification expire if someone changes firms?
faqs.a: No. The JSDA states that the qualification stays valid after leaving or moving to another member firm, unless it is revoked for a legal violation or similar reason. The person must, however, be registered again through the new firm before performing sales representative duties, and renewal training timing then applies.

faqs.q: Can a bank employee sell investment trusts without a sales representative registration?
faqs.a: No. FIEA Article 64 applies to registered financial institutions such as banks as well as securities firms. Any officer or employee who solicits or sells covered products must be registered, and Article 64(2) prohibits the firm from letting unregistered people perform those duties.

faqs.q: What happens if renewal training is not completed on time?
faqs.a: The JSDA states that the qualification is suspended if training is not completed within the period set by its rules, and that all qualifications are revoked if the person still does not complete training during the suspension. A suspended representative cannot lawfully continue sales representative duties.

faqs.q: Who handles sales representative registration, the FSA or the JSDA?
faqs.a: Registration is a power of the Prime Minister under FIEA Article 64, exercised through the Financial Services Agency. Article 64-7 allows that work to be delegated to an authorized association, and the JSDA performs registration for its members' representatives under that delegation.

FIEA Article 64-2(1) refusal grounds include revocation under Article 64-5 within five years and existing registration with another firm; Article 64-3 deemed authority for out of court acts
FIEA Article 64-5 allows revocation or suspension of duties for up to two years; Article 64-7 allows delegation of registration work to an authorized association

JSDA: qualification granted on passing the exam; registration through the member firm; JSDA performs registration under delegation from the state; qualification survives job changes; special member Class 1, 2 and 4 not valid for securities companies

JSDA: six qualification types; Class 2 excludes margin and derivatives; Class 1 covers all securities; investment trust and bond qualification abolished 31 March 2002 with a Class 2 carve-out for 1999 to 2002 certification training

JSDA: renewal training mandatory every five years from registration date and within 180 days for new or re-registered representatives; non-completion suspends the qualification and continued non-completion revokes all qualifications; persons not attached to a member are not subject
